citingPaper.title: LabWorld: Learning Interactive 4D Worlds for Scientific Experimentation

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36592, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: Autonomous scientific agents must not only reason about experiments but also interact with the physical environments in which they are executed. Existing laboratory simulators typically rely on manually constructed assets and predefined procedures, while laboratory videos capture real equipment, layouts, and interactions but leave this information implicit in pixels. We introduce LabWorld, an agent-driven Real2Sim framework for reconstructing interactive 4D laboratory worlds from monocular RGB video. LabWorld recovers reusable 3D assets, a metric scene, time-varying object states, and procedure events. Multi-frame observations provide complementary evidence for asset and scene reconstruction, while motion reconstruction combines visual and geometric observations with event constraints encoding the spatial and temporal requirements of laboratory interactions. We evaluate LabWorld on real pipetting and vortexing videos collected in our laboratory against general-purpose agentic and dedicated reconstruction baselines. For pipetting, LabWorld achieves a mean Mask IoU of 0.501, exceeding the strongest baseline by 0.033. For vortexing, it achieves a mean Tube-Length-Normalized PCK-AUC of 0.638, exceeding the strongest baseline by 0.035. On five pipetting videos, event-conditioned reconstruction increases the fraction of modeled physical constraints satisfied from 14.3% (5/35) to 100% (35/35). The resulting worlds expose geometry, motion, articulation, and events as explicit, editable state for replay, inspection, and future embodied scientific systems.

citingPaper.title: VPR-Space: A Benchmark for Visual Place Recognition in Space Analog Domains

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35642, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: Visual Place Recognition (VPR) is an important means for loop closure detection in visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM). While state-of-the-art VPR and SLAM approaches excel in urban and feature-rich natural environments, the vast and feature-poor environments of extraterrestrial surfaces like on the Moon or Mars pose severe challenges for existing approaches. This paper presents a novel benchmark, VPR-Space, to evaluate VPR capabilities on extraterrestrial surfaces. There are three contributions: (1) We collected sixteen VPR database-query datasets based on existing data from Space Analog Domains (SAD), terrestrial environments that resemble properties of the Moon or Mars. The collection includes a range of challenges regarding environment, viewpoint change, and illumination conditions. (2) To address the ill-posed nature of VPR, we propose a novel approach to generate the ground-truth information in VPR benchmarks. Instead of defining that a query and datbase image show the same place if and only if their camera poses are within fixed position and viewing direction thresholds, we propose to make the decision dependent on whether the match would be valuable in the downstream SLAM task. To avoid the overhead and restrictions of evaluating VPR in-the-loop within SLAM systems, we provide VPR ground-truth (GT) matrices based on the performance of an ensemble of state-of-the-art Relative Pose Estimators (RPE). Under this GT we require a VPR method to identify exactly those image pairs for which a subsequently applied RPE is expected to provide a valuable pose estimate in a SLAM context. (3) We evaluated nine state-of-the-art VPR approaches. The results show considerable room for improvement and indicate directions for future research. We provide a pre-release version of the dataset on github: $\texttt{https://github.com/rfechner/VPR-Space}$

citingPaper.title: Does VGGT Know What It Does Not Know?

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35806, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models such as VGGT regress cameras and geometry in a single forward pass, but they report no uncertainty for the camera poses they predict: an incorrect relative pose looks no different from a correct one. We ask whether the frozen model nonetheless knows when its pose is wrong. On HardMatch, a benchmark of 1,000 deliberately difficult image pairs on which VGGT fails on 35% of pairs, a linear probe on VGGT's frozen features predicts pose failure on held-out categories with ROC-AUC 93.5%, compared with 79.7% for VGGT's own point-map confidence and 77.7% for a classifier trained on all of VGGT's outputs. The probe catches failures VGGT is confident about, lets a downstream system abstain on the pairs it distrusts, and transfers without retraining to rotation failures on PhotoTourism and ScanNet-1500, beyond what co-visibility explains. This knowledge is absent from the per-image encoder: it is computed partway through the layers that fuse the two views, and the same holds for a second model, $\pi^3$. In essence, we find that VGGT knows more about its own failures than it reports.

citingPaper.title: Any3R: Feedforward 3D Reconstruction from Any Camera Type

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36150, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: Geometry foundation models recover camera poses and dense geometry from a set of images with a feed-forward network, but they expect pinhole images. That assumption is inside the backbone too: the positional encoding and the training loss both bind an image position to a direction in space, and both depend on the lens. We condition both on the dense ray field, the unit direction through every pixel, which describes any central camera without a lens type, distortion coefficients or a bound on field of view. Angular coordinates give the rotary encoding the measured ray angle of each patch, evaluated per view, and solid-angle weighting scales the point loss by the area each pixel covers on the sphere, so neither the encoding nor the supervision depends on the lens. Any3R is therefore a feed-forward model that takes any central camera, and is robust to mixing many camera types per scene, with no retraining per lens. On a benchmark of thirteen central cameras across three datasets, where every method reconstructs with its own predicted camera poses, it is the most consistently accurate method. Any3R enables scalable 3D reconstruction from heterogeneous crowdsourced and archival imagery collections sourced across diverse camera types. Project page: https://jingong-chen.github.io/Any3R/

citingPaper.title: ProMo3D: Probing Motion Cues in Frozen 3D Foundation Models

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33802, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: Feed-forward 3D foundation models have recently reshaped multi-view reconstruction, yet dynamic 4D understanding still often relies on large-scale motion supervision or hand-crafted, architecture-specific heuristics. We ask whether frozen 3D foundation model tokens already encode motion-relevant information that can be exposed by lightweight readout functions, rather than re-learning motion-specific features with high-capacity decoders. Through probing on three representative backbones, we find that static--dynamic separation is decodable from frozen token representations. Our rank-restricted and spectral analyses on $\pi^3$X reveal that the recovered motion cues are concentrated in a low-dimensional subspace. Building on this, we propose Probing-based Motion Distillation (PMD), which converts pairwise motion-state compatibility scores against a fixed anchor token into dense motion masks. Trained on only 160 YouTube-VOS videos using a single 16 GB GPU, PMD transfers zero-shot to DAVIS, SegTrackv2, and FBMS-59 without target-benchmark fine-tuning. With multi-view pretrained geometric backbones, PMD outperforms training-free heuristics and approaches substantially heavier supervised and self-supervised methods, suggesting that motion decoding from frozen 3D foundation models can be lightweight and data-efficient.

citingPaper.title: FlexGlue: Sparse-to-Dense Feature Matching and Visual Disambiguation

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32976, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: To estimate correspondences across images, existing approaches match either sparse interest points, which is highly efficient but limited by repeatability, or dense pixel grids, which is robust but expensive. Furthermore, these approaches are trained with only matching pairs and thus often fail to reject unrelated pairs that exhibit visual symmetries, which is equally important in applications like Structure-from-Motion (SfM). We bridge these gaps by introducing FlexGlue, a neural network for asymmetric sparse-to-dense matching and disambiguation. Given two images and coordinates of points in the first image, FlexGlue estimates the coordinates of the corresponding points in the second image while simultaneously rejecting the pair if non-matching. By searching for a limited set of correspondences among dense pixels, our approach is both fast and effective at both matching and disambiguation: it combines the sub-pixel accuracy of dense matching with the speed of sparse matching, while rejecting incorrect pairs with high precision. Experiments on multiple datasets show that FlexGlue pushes the Pareto frontier in relative pose estimation and significantly outperforms existing approaches for SfM and visual localization. FlexGlue is publicly available at https://github.com/cvg/flexglue .

citingPaper.title: Think-Capture: Active 3D Geometry Acquisition for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29232, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) excel at 2D recognition but often fail to maintain consistent 3D relations across sparse viewpoints, leading to spatial hallucinations under occlusion and perspective changes. Existing methods commonly fuse all frames with dense geometry, incurring substantial computation and context overhead while encouraging blind reliance on imperfect estimators. We present Think-Capture, a query-conditioned framework that first identifies task-critical objects and then acquires their geometry on demand. A 3D toolkit lifts zero-shot masks into a common coordinate frame, and a Symbolic 3D State Abstraction compresses object and camera states into structured text. Hierarchical Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) trains the VLM on cases in which geometry either helps or misleads, teaching it when to use tool evidence and when to fall back on visual cues. Think-Capture-4B reaches 54.4% on MindCube-Tiny (+21.5 points over its backbone), 39.1% on the MMSI-Bench positional subset (+7.9), and 42.8% on ViewSpatial (+5.2). It also remains robust under coordinate and mask perturbations. The full stack fits one 24 GB GPU and serves as an asynchronous high-level reasoner on an Agibot G1. Our code is available at https://github.com/819346675/Think-Capture.

citingPaper.title: Foundation4D: Towards a unified perception and reconstruction model for autonomous vehicles

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30340, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: We introduce Foundation4D, a unified feed-forward model for geometry estimation, 3D detection, semantic occupancy, and Gaussian reconstruction from multi-camera driving video. A shared backbone uses factorized spatiotemporal attention to efficiently combine observations across cameras and time. Our video inference pipeline uses pose graph optimization to refine camera trajectories and assembles object tracks across input windows. We also develop a data annotation pipeline and release PAI-Foundation4D, a benchmark with dense depth and semantic occupancy labels for 1,253 driving clips. With benchmark-specific fine-tuning, Foundation4D achieves the lowest depth AbsRel on Waymo and nuScenes, the highest detection mAP on nuScenes, and the highest occupancy mIoU on OpenOccupancy among the compared methods. Our task-combination study shows benefits for both detection and geometry: co-training detection with geometry and occupancy improves top-class mAP by 1.2 points over detection-only training, while co-training geometry with detection reduces camera-to-rig translation error by $13.4\%$ relative to geometry-only training. We further use the predicted geometry and trajectories as priors for lidarless NuRec, supporting reconstruction of driving scenes for simulation.

citingPaper.title: AEON: Unifying Video and 3D World Models

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28631, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: Current world models for explicit world simulation typically follow two distinct pathways: (1) video generative models (e.g., Sora), which simulate realistic appearances but fail to preserve 3D consistency; and (2) 3D generative models (e.g., Marble), which generate geometrically consistent scenes but often yield static, less realistic observations. We present AEON, a unified framework that bridges video-based and 3D-based world models and combines the benefits of both. The key insight of AEON lies in a generative model that operates within the text- or image-conditioned video latent space while producing renderable 4D graphics primitives---specifically, 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS)---as the explicit world representation. We train a 4D reconstruction model to predict both 4DGS and camera poses from monocular videos, serving as our initialized 4D decoder. Furthermore, we design a domain adapter that translates generative video latents into reconstructive 4D latents through a distillation process on the video VAE. AEON naturally supports video-based world modeling by rendering 4DGS at predicted camera trajectories, and constructs a persistent 4D environment with scene dynamics for realistic world simulation. Consequently, AEON empowers a diverse range of world modeling applications and achieves state-of-the-art performance on standard benchmarks. Project Page: https://weiqi-zhang.github.io/AEON

citingPaper.title: VitronEdit: Universal Visual Editing across Images, Videos, and 3D Scenes

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27049, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: Recent advances in unified visual editing have begun to consolidate image and video editing within a single model, while 3D scene editing remains largely separate and constrained by scarce paired training data. Given the rich image and video editing supervision now available and the common editing semantics shared across modalities, a natural question is whether this knowledge can be transferred to data-scarce 3D editing. We present VitronEdit, a universal framework for image, video, and 3D scene editing. VitronEdit adopts a shared sequence representation and progressive multimodal training to transfer editing knowledge across modalities. We further introduce geometry-aware post-training, which leverages a pretrained geometry reconstruction model to provide depth and camera-pose supervision. Surprisingly, applying geometric supervision only to 3D samples yields the best overall performance, while image and video editing also improve despite receiving no direct geometric supervision, suggesting that geometric regularization transfers through the shared backbone. Our analysis further shows that image and video training mainly transfers editing semantics to 3D, whereas 3D supervision primarily improves multi-view consistency. The project page: https://vitron-llm.github.io/VitronEdit/.

citingPaper.title: ReDT: Resolution-Decoupled Visual Geometry Transformer

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25517, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: We introduce ReDT, a feed-forward visual geometry transformer designed to scale multi-view reconstruction to high-definition (HD) inputs. Existing visual geometry transformers are typically trained at fixed, standard definition (SD) resolutions and exhibit degraded reconstruction quality and poor computational scaling to high input resolutions. While recent efficient architectures reduce the complexity of inter-frame attention, expensive intra-frame and encoder attention remain largely unaddressed, making HD reconstruction impractical with existing architectures. ReDT addresses both limitations with a resolution-aware architecture designed to scale to high-resolution inputs. The key idea of ReDT is to first map each view to a fixed-size set of basis tokens, compute correspondences in this compact constant-size basis space, and then project the outputs back to the original resolution for dense prediction. By decoupling the internal representation from input resolution during attention, ReDT substantially reduces the computational cost of high-resolution 3D reconstruction and improves model performance at all resolutions. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets spanning SD to FHD (2K) show that ReDT outperforms state-of-the-art visual geometry transformers in both reconstruction quality and computational efficiency. For instance, on the ETH3D (2K) dataset, ReDT achieves a $16\times$ speedup, a $34\%$ reduction in peak GPU memory usage, and a $33\%$ reduction in chamfer distance over VGGT-$\Omega$. \href{https://redt.github.io}{Project Website.}

citingPaper.title: Holo4D: Holistic 4D Reconstruction as Geometric Control for Video Diffusion

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25276, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: Synthesizing a monocular video from a new camera trajectory requires preserving the observed scene geometry and motion while completing regions that become newly visible. Feed-forward 4D reconstructors recover the structure of the observed scene, whereas video diffusion models provide a generative prior for completing unseen content. We introduce Holo4D, a video reshooting framework that uses reconstructed 3D trajectories as a holistic source-view 4D scaffold. We project these trajectories into the requested views and encode their geometry and source appearance to guide a pretrained video diffusion model. Together with the source video and target cameras, the scaffold grounds generation in reconstructed observations while leaving unsupported regions to the generative prior. Experiments demonstrate the value of trajectory-based conditioning for camera control and novel-view synthesis. The framework accommodates different 4D reconstructors without retraining the video generator, allowing it to benefit from future advances in source reconstruction. More details can be found in our project page.

citingPaper.title: MCSplat: Multi-View Photometric and Geometric Consistent Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting for Driving Scenes

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25345, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: Driving-scene reconstruction via feed-forward Gaussian splatting from sparse multi-view images remains challenging due to two factors. First, cross-camera photometric inconsistency, caused by variations in exposure, ISP, and illumination, can be incorrectly absorbed into Gaussian geometry. Second, unreliable local geometric supervision arises from normal-based constraints near depth discontinuities. To address these issues, we present \textbf{MCSplat}, a multi-view consistent feed-forward Gaussian splatting framework for driving scenes. MCSplat constructs a canonical appearance space from depth-guided multi-camera correspondences to decouple geometry learning from camera-specific appearance. A multi-scale Bilateral Grid Transformer restores raw camera appearance from canonical renderings, enabling photometric supervision without contaminating Gaussian geometry. To improve local geometric reliability, we estimate Fisher-information-based uncertainty from photometric sensitivity and use it to adaptively weight surface-oriented self-supervision. Extensive experiments demonstrate improved reconstruction quality and generalization across driving datasets. Geometry-oriented evaluations further reveal enhanced cross-view depth consistency and local surface-normal agreement, while qualitative results show fewer geometric artifacts and more coherent structures across overlapping views.

citingPaper.title: IntriAdapt: Generalizable Intrinsic-Guided Test-Time Adaptation for Metric Geometry Estimation

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24607, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: Recovering metric 3D geometry from images is fundamentally ill-posed due to perspective projection ambiguity. Current geometry models incorporate supplied or predicted intrinsics during inference, but do not use them to supervise model adaptation. To refine these predictions, test-time adaptation (TTA) typically relies on external depth measurements. In this paper, we instead use camera intrinsics as an output-side geometric verifier. Comparing the point cloud's viewing rays with those defined by the known intrinsics yields a direct measure of geometric inconsistency. We propose \textit{IntriAdapt}, a TTA framework that minimizes this closed-form geometric residual. By optimizing a lightweight LoRA adapter on a frozen geometry foundation model, our method aligns the prediction with the specific camera model without depth sensors or external priors. We further extend this approach to video sequences, demonstrating that adapting a short sequence generalizes to other sequences captured by the same camera. The adapted model processes held-out images in a feed-forward pass, without repeating optimization for each frame. Experiments on ten single-image and seven sequence benchmarks across multiple base models show that \textit{IntriAdapt} consistently outperforms both unadapted and oracle-intrinsics baselines in metric accuracy and relative geometry.

citingPaper.title: Foundation-Model-Driven 3D Scene Graphs for Mobile Manipulation

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23622, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: Geometric and Semantic Foundation models are becoming increasingly popular tools for generating spatial maps for robots. Recent work (e.g., FOUND-IT) has leveraged these tools to construct real-time, task-driven, and open-set 3D scene graphs from a single uncalibrated camera. However, while classical robot mapping techniques have undergone extensive system demonstrations, limited work has been done to develop both the fundamental and the systems wide advancements needed to integrate these new types of robot spatial memory into a full, useable autonomy pipeline. In this paper, we bridge this gap, and in doing so we also evaluate the effectiveness and limitations of this type of 3D memory. Towards this end, we integrate FOUND-IT into a mobile manipulator platform and demonstrate it is well-suited to support multiple objectives such as object change detection, support for multiple mapping sessions, determination of navigable paths, and directly support object grasping for the task of scene re-arrangement. Furthermore, we provide nuanced insights into the effectiveness and limitations of a monocular, foundation-model-driven 3D scene graph construction system using observations from rigorous on-robot experiments. Code is available at https://github. com/MIT-SPARK/FOUND-IT.

citingPaper.title: Motion- and Gravity-Aware Feedforward 3D Reconstruction

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22177, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: Feed-forward transformer models have recently achieved strong performance in multi-view 3D reconstruction, but they still rely primarily on appearance-based attention and often struggle in dynamic scenes with weak geometric cues. In this work, we introduce a motion- and gravity-aware framework under the Learning Using Privileged Information (LUPI) paradigm. During training, residual optical flow and gravity direction are provided as privileged signals to guide geometric representation learning; during inference, the model uses standard visual inputs only. We integrate these priors into transformer backbones with lightweight architectural changes, preserving feed-forward efficiency. Experiments on standard benchmarks show consistent gains in reconstruction accuracy and robustness, especially in scenes with dynamic objects, ambiguous structure, and challenging camera motion. Our analysis further shows that the optimal injection stage is backbone-dependent: middle-layer integration is generally preferable for VGGT, while late-stage integration is more effective for {\pi}3. These results suggest that LUPI offers a practical way to inject motion and physical priors into feed-forward 3D reconstruction without increasing test-time complexity.

citingPaper.title: Velox: Spatial Memory Makes World Models Efficient

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22311, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: Video world models turn actions and camera motion into long visual rollouts, making video a natural interface for interactive simulation. Such interaction requires responsive generation, yet coherent rollouts must retain visual memory of what has already been generated. Chunked video diffusion models usually keep this context in growing KV caches, so later chunks become progressively slower. To address this bottleneck, we introduce Velox, a training-free attention router for region-level context selection using frustum slab correspondences from streaming geometry. Velox represents historical blocks as camera frustum slabs with depth intervals and obtains current-block depth through recency-priority multiwarp. For well-covered regions, frustum slab overlap softly modulates each layer's model-derived block importance. Uncovered regions retain the model-derived route without geometric bias. The fixed token-block granularity matches FlashAttention-style tiled execution and reduces the attention term that grows with rollout length. Frustum slab construction runs asynchronously with denoising on the same H200. At chunk 48, Velox accelerates attention by $4.36\times$ and denoising by $2.43\times$. On the full 158-case WBench navigation split, it remains within 0.15 API-free average points of dense LingBot-Fast-Cam. Please see our project page at https://velox-world.com/velox/ for more details.

citingPaper.title: Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22371, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: We introduce Gen4P, a unified framework for recovering 4D geometry and motion from monocular video. We show that a pretrained video generator can be repurposed into a feed-forward 4D perceiver without iterative denoising. Building on on-demand querying, Gen4P processes clean video latents in a single encoder pass and predicts the requested 4D attributes through a lightweight cross-attention decoder. The on-demand query formulation enables flexible spatial sampling, and our proposed continuous-time queries further provide temporal flexibility. To strengthen geometric knowledge, we propose a straightforward plug-in solution by incorporating a pretrained video-depth LoRA as a frozen geometry prior, improving overall performance without adding extra trainable parameters. Gen4P achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on tasks of 3D point tracking, video depth and camera pose estimation. Qualitative results on in-the-wild videos illustrate its capability of tracking complex motion while maintaining the delicate structure. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of video generative pretraining for unified 4D perception. See https://gen4p.github.io for more visual results.

citingPaper.title: From Pixels to Executable Physics: Behavior-Grounded World Models for Embodied Action Consequence Prediction

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.17630, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: In outdoor environments, varying terrain and contact conditions can cause identical action commands to produce different motion outcomes for quadruped robots. Predicting these outcomes is essential for reliable navigation and informed path selection. Existing video world models can generate visually plausible futures, yet often struggle to capture robot dynamics and terrain interactions, leading to overly optimistic predictions of action outcomes. We present DR-WM, a physically consistent world model that incorporates robot-terrain contact dynamics to predict the consequences of quadruped actions. Starting from an initial RGB image, our method reconstructs scene geometry and integrates dense, dimensionless priors over terrain contact properties, calibrated using real-world action-response data. The resulting terrain model supports the simulation of physics with spatially varying contact properties such as friction. Given the initial state of the robot and candidate action sequences, we simulate its future motion and use the resulting camera trajectories and rendered geometry to guide the training of a video world model. The generated future observations are then used to update the terrain reconstruction, enabling iterative model rollouts without additional real-world images. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DR-WM substantially outperforms geometry-only baselines and baselines with uniform physical parameters on key physical metrics characterizing action outcomes, while achieving the best performance among the evaluated baselines. These physically grounded predictions support more informed action selection: across 90 challenging scenarios, an 8B vision-language model augmented with DR-WM outperforms an unassisted 32B vision-language model on five of six evaluation metrics.

citingPaper.title: PanoGS: Foundation-Depth-Guided High-Resolution Gaussian Splatting from Sparse Panoramic Images for Interactive Web3D Exploration

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/10.1145/3822516.3834880?email=<INSERT_YOUR_EMAIL> or https://doi.org/10.1145/3822516.3834880, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: Sparse panoramic capture enables efficient indoor digitization, but transforming a few 360° images into web-based, high-resolution 3D representations remains difficult. Limited viewpoint overlap, equirectangular (ERP) distortions, uncertain depth scale, and the perspective-camera assumptions of most image-to-3D pipelines make direct reconstruction unreliable. This paper introduces PanoGS, a pipeline that uses inferred depth from vision foundation models to guide the generation of high-resolution 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes from sparse panoramic images. Given a small set of RGB panoramas, we first estimate camera poses and low-resolution depth priors using a feed-forward panoramic reconstruction model. We then refine these priors at native ERP resolution through global-local depth refinement and fuse the resulting RGB-D panoramas into a Truncated Signed Distance Function (TSDF) geometric substrate, which provides stable surface support, normals, visibility information, and local scale estimates for initializing anisotropic Gaussian primitives. The initialized scene is further refined using an ERP-aware Gaussian optimization strategy with progressive levels of detail, appearance warm-start, conservative geometry updates, neighbor-based multiview refinement, and shardwise processing for large scenes. The resulting assets can be exported to Gaussian splat viewers and browser-based inspection tools. Results on indoor panoramic scenes demonstrate that the proposed guided formulation produces more stable and complete Gaussian scenes than direct depth-based seeding. At the same time, high-resolution depth refinement improves fine geometric and visual detail. PanoGS shows how sparse 360° captures can be transformed into practical web-based Gaussian representations for Web3D applications. 1

citingPaper.title: WorldRoPE: Probabilistic World-Centric Rotary Embedding for Multi-View Attention

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16337, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: Rotary Positional Embedding (RoPE) is widely used to encode relative positions in Transformers. In multi-view settings, however, patch coordinates are defined independently in each image: the same 3D point can therefore have different coordinates across views, making them insufficient for establishing cross-view correspondences. We introduce WorldRoPE, a probabilistic world-centric RoPE for multi-view attention. At each layer, WorldRoPE back-projects each patch token into a set of volumetric Gaussian primitives in a shared world frame. These primitives represent multiple plausible 3D supports for a token, jointly capturing alternative depth hypotheses, depth uncertainty, and the finite spatial extent of its patch frustum. When a key token's support is projected into a query view, it induces a distribution over where that key may appear in the query image. WorldRoPE integrates the rotary operator over this distribution in closed form, combining rotations at the projected primitive centers according to their mixture weights with covariance-dependent attenuation. This makes attention less sensitive to uncertain key locations in the query view, without rasterizing or warping token features. The formulation reduces to deterministic RoPE when the support collapses to a point. Across layers, the predicted geometry guides cross-view attention, while the updated features refine the geometry used at the next layer. Experiments on novel view synthesis, depth estimation, and 3D geometry reconstruction demonstrate the effectiveness of WorldRoPE for multi-view Transformers.

citingPaper.title: UniMetric: Universal Metric Scale Recovery for Visual Geometry Foundation Models

citingPaper.abstract: Recent advances in multimodal foundation models, exemplified by GPT-6 Astra, raise the prospect of general-purpose embodied reasoning and planning. To address these limitations, we propose CROSS, a unified cross-view localization framework built upon 3D-grounded alignment, structure-aware matching, and hypothesis ranking. This formulation makes structure learning an intrinsic requirement, encourages semantic representations to remain stable, and enables the model to acquire transferable geometry. citingPaper.abstract: Visual localization -- estimating a camera pose within a pre-existing map -- is a fundamental problem in computer vision. Existing methods address this gap through data-driven learning, yet they require large-scale training data and environment-specific retraining, limiting their practical deployment. We propose a zero-shot floorplan localization method that generalizes to novel environments without any retraining. Our key insight is that dominant geometric primitives -- lines and circles -- are ubiquitous in human-made environments and provide appearance-invariant structural constraints. We extract these primitives from a bird's-eye-view (BEV) projection of monocular 3D reconstructions and match them to the floorplan via dedicated minimal solvers within a robust estimation framework. Experiments on both simulated and real-world datasets show that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art learning-based methods on unseen environments, while using a single fixed set of hyperparameters across all experiments. citingPaper.abstract: Feed-forward models for 3D reconstruction have achieved strong performance using deep cross-view attention to exchange information across images. Inspired by BA, we propose BA-T, an iterative Transformer that implements BA-style structured updates as a repeatable layer in implicit token space. citingPaper.abstract: Despite advances in depth estimation, flying points remain a persistent failure mode: near object boundaries, depth estimators often predict spurious 3D points in the empty space between foreground and background surfaces. A model that predicts a single depth cannot keep both possibilities, so training instead pulls the prediction toward an intermediate depth that lies on neither surface. We address this with MDA, a mixture-density representation that lets the model predict multiple depth hypotheses and their associated probabilities for each pixel. Near boundaries, different hypotheses can align with different surfaces, and the decoded depth is selected from one of these hypotheses rather than placed in the empty space between them. Across different architectures, MDA substantially improves boundary reconstruction over each base model and largely removes flying-point artifacts even under severe input blur, while adding negligible runtime overhead. citingPaper.abstract: The Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer (VGGT) marks a significant leap forward in 3D scene reconstruction, as it is the first model that directly infers all key 3D attributes (camera poses, depths, and dense geometry) jointly in one pass. citingPaper.abstract: 3D reconstruction from multi-view images is a core challenge in computer vision. However, this approach suffers from poor scalability due to the quadratic complexity of self-attention and the large number of tokens generated in long image sequences. In this work, we introduce FlashVGGT, an efficient alternative that addresses this bottleneck through a descriptor-based attention mechanism. Instead of applying dense global attention across all tokens, FlashVGGT compresses spatial information from each frame into a compact set of descriptor tokens. Global attention is then computed as cross-attention between the full set of image tokens and this smaller descriptor set, significantly reducing computational overhead. Moreover, the compactness of the descriptors enables online inference over long sequences via a chunk-recursive mechanism that reuses cached descriptors from previous chunks. citingPaper.abstract: Self-supervised learning on images seeks to extract meaningful visual representations from unlabeled data. citingPaper.title: Block-Sparse Global Attention for Efficient Multi-View Geometry Transformers

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.07120, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: Efficient and accurate feed-forward multi-view reconstruction has long been an important task in computer vision. Recent transformer-based models like VGGT, $\pi^3$ and MapAnything have demonstrated remarkable performance with relatively simple architectures. However, their scalability is fundamentally constrained by the quadratic complexity of global attention, which imposes a significant runtime bottleneck when processing large image sets. In this work, we empirically analyze the global attention matrix of these models and observe that the probability mass concentrates on a small subset of patch-patch interactions corresponding to cross-view geometric correspondences. Building on this insight and inspired by recent advances in large language models, we propose a training-free, block-sparse replacement for dense global attention, implemented with highly optimized kernels. Our method accelerates inference by more than $3\times$ while maintaining comparable task performance. Evaluations on a comprehensive suite of multi-view benchmarks demonstrate that our approach seamlessly integrates into existing global attention-based architectures such as VGGT, $\pi^3$ , and MapAnything, while substantially improving scalability to large image collections.

citingPaper.title: CHROMA: Consistent Harmonization of Multi-View Appearance via Bilateral Grid Prediction

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.15748, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: Modern camera pipelines apply extensive on-device processing, such as exposure adjustment, white balance, and color correction, which, while beneficial individually, often introduce photometric inconsistencies across views. These appearance variations violate multi-view consistency and degrade novel view synthesis. Joint optimization of scene-specific representations and per-image appearance embeddings has been proposed to address this issue, but with increased computational complexity and slower training. In this work, we propose a generalizable, feed-forward approach that predicts spatially adaptive bilateral grids to correct photometric variations in a multi-view consistent manner. Our model processes hundreds of frames in a single step, enabling efficient large-scale harmonization, and seamlessly integrates into downstream 3D reconstruction models, providing cross-scene generalization without requiring scene-specific retraining. To overcome the lack of paired data, we employ a hybrid self-supervised rendering loss leveraging 3D foundation models, improving generalization to real-world variations. Extensive experiments show that our approach outperforms or matches the reconstruction quality of existing scene-specific optimization methods with appearance modeling, without significantly affecting the training time of baseline 3D models.

citingPaper.abstract: We introduce MetricHMSR, a novel framework for recovering metric human meshes and 3D scenes from a single monocular image. Existing methods struggle to recover metric scale due to monocular scale ambiguity and weak-perspective camera assumptions. Moreover, their fully coupled feature representations make it difficult to disentangle local pose from global translation, often requiring multi-stage pipelines that introduce accumulated errors. To address these challenges, we propose MetricHMR (Metric Human Mesh Recovery), which incorporates a bounding camera ray map representation to provide explicit metric cues for human reconstruction,together with a Human Mixture-of-Experts (HumanMoE) that dynamically routes image features to specialized experts, enabling the disentangled perception of local human pose and global metric position. Leveraging the recovered metric human as a geometric anchor, we further refine monocular metric depth estimation to achieve more accurate 3D alignment between humans and scenes.Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on both human mesh recovery and metric human-scene reconstruction. citingPaper.title: UFM: A Simple Path towards Unified Dense Correspondence with Flow

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09278, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: Dense image correspondence is central to many applications, such as visual odometry, 3D reconstruction, object association, and re-identification. Historically, dense correspondence has been tackled separately for wide-baseline scenarios and optical flow estimation, despite the common goal of matching content between two images. In this paper, we develop a Unified Flow&Matching model (UFM), which is trained on unified data for pixels that are co-visible in both source and target images. UFM uses a simple, generic transformer architecture that directly regresses the (u,v) flow. It is easier to train and more accurate for large flows compared to the typical coarse-to-fine cost volumes in prior work. UFM is 28% more accurate than state-of-the-art flow methods (Unimatch), while also having 62% less error and 6.7x faster than dense wide-baseline matchers (RoMa). UFM is the first to demonstrate that unified training can outperform specialized approaches across both domains. This result enables fast, general-purpose correspondence and opens new directions for multi-modal, long-range, and real-time correspondence tasks.

citingPaper.title: SpatialScore: Towards Comprehensive Evaluation for Spatial Intelligence

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.17012, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: Existing evaluations of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on spatial intelligence are typically fragmented and limited in scope. In this work, we aim to conduct a holistic assessment of the spatial understanding capabilities of modern MLLMs and propose complementary data-driven and agent-based solutions. Specifically, we make the following contributions: (i) we introduce SpatialScore, to our knowledge, the most comprehensive and diverse benchmark for multimodal spatial intelligence to date. It covers multiple visual data types, input modalities, and question-answering formats, and contains approximately 5K manually verified samples spanning 30 distinct tasks; (ii) using SpatialScore, we extensively evaluate 49 representative MLLMs, revealing persistent challenges and a substantial gap between current models and human-level spatial intelligence; (iii) to advance model capabilities, we construct SpatialCorpus, a large-scale training resource with 331K multimodal QA samples that supports fine-tuning on spatial reasoning tasks and significantly improves the performance of existing models (e.g., Qwen3-VL); (iv) to complement this data-driven route with a training-free paradigm, we develop SpatialAgent, a multi-agent system equipped with 12 specialized spatial perception tools that supports both Plan-Execute and ReAct reasoning, enabling substantial gains in spatial reasoning without additional model training. Extensive experiments and in-depth analyses demonstrate the effectiveness of our benchmark, corpus, and agent framework. We expect these resources to serve as a solid foundation for advancing MLLMs toward human-level spatial intelligence. All data, code, and models will be released to the research community.

citingPaper.title: Loop Closure From Two Views: Revisiting PGO for Scalable Trajectory Estimation Through Monocular Priors

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.16275, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: (Visual) Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) remains a fundamental challenge in enabling autonomous systems to navigate and understand large-scale environments. Traditional SLAM approaches struggle to balance efficiency and accuracy, particularly in large-scale settings where extensive computational resources are required for scene reconstruction and Bundle Adjustment (BA). However, this scene reconstruction, in the form of sparse pointclouds of visual landmarks, is often only used within the SLAM system because navigation and planning methods require different map representations. In this work, we therefore investigate a more scalable Visual SLAM (VSLAM) approach without reconstruction, mainly based on approaches for two-view loop closures. By restricting the map to a sparse keyframed pose graph without dense geometry representations, our ‘2GO’ system achieves efficient optimization with competitive absolute trajectory accuracy. In particular, we find that recent advancements in image matching and monocular depth priors enable very accurate trajectory optimization without BA. We conduct extensive experiments on diverse datasets, including large-scale scenarios, and provide a detailed analysis of the trade-offs between runtime, accuracy, and map size. Our results demonstrate that this streamlined approach supports real-time performance, scales well in map size and trajectory duration, and effectively broadens the capabilities of VSLAM for long-duration deployments to large environments.

citingPaper.title: Test-Time 3D Occupancy Prediction

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.08485, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: Self-supervised 3D occupancy prediction offers a promising solution for understanding complex driving scenes without requiring costly 3D annotations. However, training dense occupancy decoders to capture fine-grained geometry and semantics can demand hundreds of GPU hours, and once trained, such models struggle to adapt to varying voxel resolutions or novel object categories without extensive retraining. To overcome these limitations, we propose a practical and flexible test-time occupancy prediction framework termed TT-Occ. Our method incrementally constructs, optimizes, and voxelizes time-aware 3D Gaussians from raw sensor streams by integrating vision foundation models (VFMs) at runtime. The flexible representation of 3D Gaussians enables voxelization at arbitrary user-specified resolutions, while the strong generalization capability of VFMs supports accurate perception and open-vocabulary recognition without requiring any network training or fine-tuning. To validate the generality and effectiveness of our framework, we present two variants: a LiDAR-based version and a vision-centric version, and conduct extensive experiments on the Occ3D-nuScenes and nuCraft benchmarks under varying voxel resolutions. Experimental results show that TT-Occ significantly outperforms existing computationally expensive pretrained self-supervised counterparts. Code is available at https://github.com/Xian-Bei/TT-Occ.

citingPaper.title: Image Matching Filtering and Refinement by Planes and Beyond

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.09484, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: This paper provides a consistent and extensive evaluation of state-of-the-art filtering and refinement methods on common image matching pipelines. Unlike previous comparisons, the designed benchmark also takes into account the more general, real, and practical cases where camera intrinsics are unavailable. Moreover, a novel and effective strategy combining non-deep traditional computer vision approaches based on planar constraints and cross correlation is presented. Experimental analysis provides several insights for current application design and future research directions. In particular, the choice of a proper evaluation protocol discloses the effective differences within the compared solutions which otherwise would tend to flatten. Moreover, the proposed classical algorithmic approach is competitive with recent deep methods. Besides providing robust baseline using traditional computer vision for the evaluation of deep-based methods, this knowledge is useful to improve and better understand the deep image matching architectures. On one hand, geometry-based filtering is effective in presence of outliers without degrading already robust deep pipelines; on the other hand cross-correlation refinement is valid in the case of corner-like keypoints and allows to not directly discard inaccurate matches by default in deep pipelines but to retain and refine them for achieving a better coverage of the scene.

citingPaper.title: Learning-Based Multi-View Stereo: A Survey

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.15235, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

citingPaper.abstract: 3D reconstruction aims to recover the dense 3D structure of a scene. It plays an essential role in various applications such as Augmented/Virtual Reality (AR/VR), autonomous driving and robotics. Leveraging multiple views of a scene captured from different viewpoints, Multi-View Stereo (MVS) algorithms synthesize a comprehensive 3D representation, enabling precise reconstruction in complex environments. Due to its efficiency and effectiveness, MVS has become a pivotal method for image-based 3D reconstruction. Recently, with the success of deep learning, many learning-based MVS methods have been proposed, achieving impressive performance against traditional methods. We categorize these learning-based methods as: depth map-based, voxel-based, NeRF-based, 3D Gaussian Splatting-based, and large feed-forward methods. Among these, we focus significantly on depth map-based methods, which are the main family of MVS due to their conciseness, flexibility and scalability. In this survey, we provide a comprehensive review of the literature at the time of this writing. We investigate these learning-based methods, summarize their performances on popular benchmarks, and discuss promising future research directions in this area.

citingPaper.abstract: : The rapid rise of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools in recent years has resulted in exciting new possibilities for computer programmers, game and web developers, and three-dimensional (3D) art practitioners. In particular, algorithms that use AI techniques to infer structure from a series of still images, have very quickly had a profound effect upon the landscape of computer and web graphics, and can now be found in domains including cinematic visual effects, architecture, design, advertising, and heritage. Of interest in this study are what we call 3D mini-maps (3DMM): stylized reality captures that enable interactive, full-perspective exploration. This position paper takes the following two stances: 1) creating 3DMM’s from scratch is both tedious and difficult, requiring technical and design skills, but still offers high rewards; and 2) Large Language Model agents are rapidly gaining traction as a powerful means of automation and could be turned loose on the task of generating a 3DMM.
